name: Neenerinathar Temple, Tiruthandalaineeneri (Thandalaicherry)
deity: Shiva as Neenerinathar, with the goddess Gnanambikai
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Thandalaicherry, the Tevaram's Tiruthandalaineeneri, near Thiruthuraipoondi, honours Shiva as Neenerinathar with the goddess Gnanambikai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, it is revered as the birthplace of Arivattaya Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Nayanmars, whose steadfast offering of food to Shiva is among the most moving of Shaiva stories.

sections.history: Thandalaicherry, whose Tevaram name is Tiruthandalaineeneri, lies about 3–4 km north of Thiruthuraipoondi on the road toward Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, counted among the Shiva shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The village is cherished as the birthplace of Arivattaya Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Nayanmars. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Neenerinathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Gnanambikai — 'mother of wisdom' — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the kurundham, and the sacred tank is the Omaka Theertham. The temple keeps the simple, well-ordered plan of the smaller Kaveri-bank sanctuaries.
sections.legends: The village is above all the birthplace of Arivattaya Nayanar, a devotee who prepared cooked rice each day as an offering and carried it to the lord. One day, worn by age and the long path, he stumbled and the offering spilled; in anguish that his service had failed, he raised his sickle to end his life — and Shiva, moved by his devotion, stayed his hand and received the offering, taking him into grace. The goddess Gnanambikai, mother of wisdom, presides beside Neenerinathar, keeping this a shrine of steadfast, selfless devotion.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), the festival of Arivattaya Nayanar, Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims honouring the sixty-three Nayanmars include Thandalaicherry among their stops.
sections.experience: At Thandalaicherry the pilgrim comes to the home of Arivattaya Nayanar, whose love fed the lord each day. Before Neenerinathar and Gnanambikai, beside the Omaka Theertham, the visitor feels the tenderness of a shrine where devotion was so steadfast that Shiva himself would not let it fail.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thandalaicherry is about 3–4 km north of Thiruthuraipoondi on the road toward Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district (Velur post, PIN 614715). Thiruthuraipoondi is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
